title: 6.2.4 Lab: Take the shot
description: Pull back from the cue ball and let go: the ball crosses the table, and the rails stop it.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The table and the rails are there. The ball does not move.

steps.title: Aim and shoot
steps.instructions: Add the held line and the release shot from 6.2.3. The ball should leave the cue and cross the table.

steps.title: Prove the cap
steps.instructions: Pull far outside the table and let go: the shot must be the same as a shorter maximum pull.
hints: If it is faster, the cap is missing or applied after the speed.

requirements.title: A shot on release
requirements.description: Direction and speed are set inside a mouse.released() test. Help: 6.2.1 (Reading: Which way, how fast)

requirements.title: Power from the pull, capped
requirements.description: Speed comes from the distance and is capped. Help: 6.2.1 (Reading: Which way, how fast)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Lab: Take the shot". The task: turn a pull-back into a shot: a line while held, then direction away from the pointer and speed from the capped pull, on release. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: Shot on release
rubric.description: The release is what sets the shot.

rubric.title: Direction away
rubric.description: The direction is the angle to the pointer plus 180 (or the equivalent).
